I recently bought a Gigabyte R9 390x, but I find that when I run a game or benchmark my pc crashes with a frozen sound studder. I limited the GPU power settings by 50%(maximum value allowed) and downclocked by 42.8%, by doing so the instability seems to have been rectified.

The r9 390x recommends a 750w PSU and currently I have a Cooler Master SILENT Pro 600w psu. I have an 850w psu ordered but while I wait for it to be delivered I figured I'd do some trouble shooting.

The GPU has a TDP of 275w

CPU FX-8120 has a TDP of 125

Fans 1x140mm 2x120mm TDP = 18w

HDD = 9W

RAM 4GBx2 = 6w

MOBO = 80w

Total 518w (RAM, HDD, MOBO, Fans were calculated using the maximum values for typical component power consumption, thus it is a liberal estimation)

Short of the 600w psu that has a max limit of 720w, one thing I have noticed however is that the GPU requires a 6pin+8pin connection, the PSU has two 6+2pin connectors but they are coming out of a 6pin slot (as opposed to the 850w psu I ordered which has 8pin slots on the rear) I was wondering if that could cause the instability?
